test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 26th July 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Directions: Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Are the attendance rules being relaxed by the authorities?

options.text: Have the authorities been relaxing the attendance rules?
Have the authorities relaxed the attendance rules?
Are the authorities going to relax the attendance rules?
Are the authorities relaxing the attendance rules?

solution: The correct answer is '**Are the authorities relaxing the attendance rules?**' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action. • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence. • The given sentence is in the passive voice and it is in the present continuous tense. • When we convert this sentence into an active voice, the subject '**the attendance rules**' of the passive voice becomes the object, the object 'the authorities' becomes the subject. • The passive format "are + being + V3 (relaxed)" should be converted into the active format "are + **present participle form of the verb** (relaxing)". • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present continuous tense. Hence, the correct answer is option 4. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table: TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** • Active Voice में, एक वाक्य विषय पर जोर देता है, एक क्रिया करता है। • Passive Voice में, एक वाक्य वाक्य की क्रिया या वस्तु पर जोर देता है। • दिया गया वाक्य passive voice में है और यह present continuous tense में है। • जब हम इस वाक्य को active voice में बदलते हैं, तो passive voice का subject 'the attendance rules', object बन जाता है और object 'the authorities', subject बन जाता है। • Passive format "are + being + V3 (relaxed)" को active format "are + present participle form of the verb (relaxing)" में परिवर्तित किया जाना चाहिए। • यह present continuous tense के लिए active and passive voice rule है। अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है। 84:T1896, The correct answer is '**me whether I had seen**.'
